translations.text: Simon Peter, the servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to those who have received faith as precious as ours through the righteousness of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior.
May grace and peace increase for you through the knowledge of our Lord Jesus.
Through his holy power he has given us everything that leads to life and devotion to God, through the knowledge of the one who [?] by his glory and goodness.
Through these he has given you the great and precious promises, so that through them you may share in the holy nature, having escaped the desire for corruption that is in the world.
And in this also, putting forth every effort, add goodness to your faith, and knowledge to goodness,
and self-control to knowledge, endurance to self-control, and devotion to God to endurance,
and love for fellow believers to devotion to God, and love to love for fellow believers.
For if these things are yours and are increasing, they will not leave you idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For anyone who does not have these things is blind and cannot see, having forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.

For this reason, brothers and sisters, make even greater efforts so that through good deeds you may establish for yourselves a firm faith, together with your calling and your election. For if you do these things, you will never fall.
For in this way you will be richly provided with a way to enter the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior.
For this reason I will always take care to remind you of these things, although you know them and are firmly established in the truth that is present.
I consider it right, as long as I am in this dwelling, to stir you up by reminding you,
knowing that I will soon lay aside my body, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has told me.
I will also make every effort so that after my departure you may always keep these things in mind.
For we did not follow cleverly constructed stories when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Rather, we had seen his greatness.
For he received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice like this came to him from the great glory: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am pleased.”
And we ourselves heard this voice coming from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the firmly established word of the prophet. You do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp burning in a dark place, until the day shines and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Understand this first: no prophecy of Scripture has its interpretation on its own.
For prophecy was not brought forth at this time by human will. Rather, the holy people of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.
But false prophets arose, just as false teachers will arise among you. They will introduce destructive heresies and deny the Lord who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves.
And many will follow their defilements, and because of them the glory of the kingdom will be slandered.
And in their greed they will exploit you with deceptive words. Their judgment has not withdrawn from them since the beginning, and their destruction will not slumber.
For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but threw them down into the abyss, into unfathomable darkness, and handed them over to be kept for judgment while they are being punished,
And he did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, one of eight, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly.
And he burned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, condemning them to destruction and making them an example for those who would act wickedly.
And he rescued righteous Lot, who was being oppressed by the filthy deeds of the lawless.
For he was a righteous man, and as he lived among them, what he saw and heard day after day tormented his righteous soul with their lawless deeds.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to keep sinners for the day of judgment to punish them.
Especially those who have followed the flesh in defiling desire and have despised authority. They are bold and self-willed, and they do not tremble before glory when they speak abusively of it.
Whereas angels, who are greater in power and strength, do not bring an abusive judgment against them.
These people, born like creatures of instinct to be captured and destroyed, speak abusively of things they do not understand. They will perish in their own destruction.
They have received the wages of wrongdoing. They consider indulgence in the daytime a pleasure. They are stains and blemishes, indulging themselves and delighting in their deceptions.
Their eyes are full of adultery, and they never stop sinning. They deceive the souls of those who are unstable. They have trained their hearts in greed. They are children of the curse.
They have gone astray and abandoned the straight path, following the path of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing.
But he received a rebuke for his own lawlessness: an animal unable to speak [?] humans answered and restrained the prophet’s foolishness.
These people are springs with no water in them and clouds driven by a storm. Gloomy darkness has been reserved for them.
For they speak empty boasts and, through the desires of the flesh and filthy conduct, deceive those who have barely escaped from those who live in error.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to corruption. For a person is a slave to whatever overpowers them.

For if they have escaped the world’s defilements through the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior, but become entangled in them again and fall, their final condition has become worse than their first.
For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to know it and turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
The words of the true proverb have come upon them: “A dog has returned to its vomit,” and, “A sow that has washed herself returns to rolling in the mud.”
Look, my beloved, this is the second letter I am writing to you. In these letters I stir up your pure mind by reminding you,
so that you may remember the words spoken beforehand through the holy prophets and the commandment of the apostles of our Lord and Savior.
First, understand this: in the last days mockers will come with mockery, living according to their own desires
and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For ever since our ancestors fell asleep, everything has continued as it was from the beginning of creation.”
For this is hidden from them when they say this: the heavens existed from the beginning, and the earth came into being out of water and through water by the word of God.
Through these, the world of that time was submerged in water and destroyed.
The present heavens and earth, by that same word, are stored up for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
Do not let this one thing be hidden from you, my beloved: with the Lord, a single day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a single day.
For the Lord will not delay his promise, as some say that he will delay. Rather, he is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish, but wanting everyone to repent.
But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will swiftly pass away, the elements will burn and dissolve, and the earth and the works in it will not be found.
Since all these things are dissolved in this way, what kind of people should you be in holy deeds and devotion to God?
As you look forward to and hasten toward the coming of the day of God, on which the heavens will dissolve as they burn, and the elements will burn and dissolve.
But let us look forward to new heavens and a new earth, in keeping with his promises, in which righteousness dwells.
Therefore, my beloved, as you look forward to these things, make every effort to be found spotless and undefiled before him, at peace.
And consider the patience of our Lord to be salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him.

Just as he speaks about these things in all his letters, there are statements in them that are difficult to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort, as they also distort the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
But you, my beloved, knowing this beforehand, guard yourselves so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your own firm standing.
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior. Glory to him, both now and through the days of eternity. Amen.
